description:
v2 encoder backend matrix and fallback policy locked. Full design record: N-004.

Backend matrix (live capture / rolling write):
- NVIDIA -> NVENC (h264_nvenc primary; hevc_nvenc when source supports; av1_nvenc deferred).
- AMD on Linux -> VAAPI (h264_vaapi / hevc_vaapi).
- AMD on Windows -> AMF: future path only in v2.0.0. Slot reserved, never probed, never selected. Falls through to libx264 with `encoder.fallbackEngaged(windows-amd-deferred)`.
- Intel Arc on Linux -> QSV (with VAAPI as sub-fallback). Intel iGPU gen<12 on Linux -> VAAPI only.
- Intel on Windows -> QSV.
- Universal fallback -> libx264.

At most one HW backend selected per session. Probe order is per-platform/per-vendor, single-pass, at session start only. Never mid-stream.

Capability probe = minimum real encode (init device + open encoder + encode two synthetic NV12 frames + close). Cached in $XDG_CACHE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/encoder-probe.json keyed by (platform, vendor, GPU PCI ID, driver version, kernel version, app version). Positive cache: 7 days. Negative cache: 30 days. **Negative cache hits do not retry** -- this is the explicit v1.1.0 broken-fallback-loop fix. Manual reset via `--reset-encoder-probe` or advanced settings.

Per-vendor accepted inputs: NV12 preferred everywhere; P010 only when source is 10-bit AND backend supports it AND HEVC chosen; RGB accepted with per-backend conversion cost (CUDA shader / VAAPI VPP / libswscale).

DMA-BUF import expectations: NVENC = CUDA external memory, modifier floor = LINEAR NV12; VAAPI = vaCreateSurfaces with DRM_PRIME_2, accepts Mesa-advertised modifiers; QSV = VAAPI-backed on Linux (same modifiers), D3D11 NTHANDLE on Windows; AMF = D3D11 NTHANDLE (future); libx264 = consumes SHM only.

SHM fallback policy (binding): **SHM frames go to libx264 only.** If capture is forced to SHM, encoder switches to libx264 at session start with `encoder.fallbackEngaged(shm-forced)` before any frame flows. No hardware encoder is fed SHM frames in v2.0.0. Reason: uploading SHM into a HW encoder re-creates the v1.1.0 bandwidth ceiling.

Rate control defaults (rolling replay): NVENC = CBR-HQ p5 no-lookahead bf=0; VAAPI = CBR balanced bf=0; QSV = VBR maxrate=target+25% target_usage=4 bf=0; libx264 = veryfast VBR-with-maxrate-cap. Bitrate ladder 12/25/50 Mbps H.264 and 8/18/35 Mbps HEVC for 1080p60/1440p60/4K60. vbv-bufsize = 2x target.

GOP / keyframe policy: closed GOP, length = 2 x fps (IDR every 2 s), scenecut disabled, refs=1, bf=0 during rolling capture. Force-IDR at segment boundaries and on every `formatChanged`. Open GOP refused.

PTS expectations from CaptureSource: input is `FrameHandle::pts_ns` monotonic; first-frame anchored at t0; encoder timebase = 1/90000; VFR allowed; out-of-order frames dropped (no reorder); gap events surfaced not hidden; no wall-clock anywhere; DTS == PTS for v2.0.0 (no B-frames live).

Container for rolling segment buffer: **fragmented MP4 (fMP4)**. Init segment written once via `+empty_moov`; ~250 ms fragments via `+frag_keyframe+default_base_moof+separate_moof`; T-006 may roll multiple fragments per on-disk segment file. Rejected alternatives recorded: raw ES (no PTS, needs sidecar), MPEG-TS (~2% overhead + PCR/PMT cost), Matroska (less mature concat path; export container is MP4 anyway).

Container/codec for final export: plain MP4 (`moov` at front, `+faststart`), same codec as captured. Stream copy by default. AAC-LC for audio when audio path lands.

Replay finalization / remux policy: (a) trim on IDR -> pure stream copy; (b) trim mid-GOP -> head/tail GOPs re-encoded with **libx264 only**; (c) `formatChanged` spanning trim -> cross-boundary re-encode with libx264; (d) muxer-validation failure -> full libx264 re-encode + diagnostic; (e) user "Maximum compatibility" toggle -> full libx264 re-encode. **All Linux finalisation re-encode goes through libx264. No hardware encoder is asked to re-encode.** This preserves the v1.1.0 lesson explicitly.

When Linux HW encode is used: live capture + rolling write, when probe passed, when DMA-BUF was negotiated. When Linux HW finalisation falls back to libx264: every re-encode case in §13 of N-004 -- categorically. HW for live, CPU for re-encode. No exceptions.

Diagnostics counters (per stream, 1 Hz tick + state-change events): backend, state, fragment_index, gop_count, idr_forced_total / idr_unforced_total, frames_in / encoded / dropped_back_pressure / dropped_format_mismatch / dropped_pts_regression, pts_gap_events_total, encode_latency_ms p50/p95/p99, bitrate_observed_kbps, bitrate_target_kbps, vbv_underruns_total, dmabuf_import_success_total / dmabuf_import_failure_total, shm_copy_bytes_total, convert_cost_ms_per_frame, hwenc_runtime_errors_total, encoder_uptime_ms. Pairs with N-003 §14 capture counters and T-006 segment counters so a dropped frame can be attributed to capture vs encode vs segment write without re-running.

Error/failure reason codes: encoder-probe-failed, encoder-init-failed, encoder-format-rejected, encoder-import-failed, encoder-runtime-error, encoder-disconnected, encoder-back-pressure (diagnostic only, not fatal), encoder-fallback-engaged (informational). Every sessionLost carries backend + last-encoded count + latency p99 + last 30 s of encoder counters in $XDG_STATE_HOME/cove-screen-recorder/diagnostics/<sessionId>.json.

Encoder fallback reporting (loud, never silent): `encoder.probeResult` (full matrix) + `encoder.selected` (chosen backend + codec) + `encoder.fallbackEngaged` (reason: no-hw-vendor | probe-failed | shm-forced | negative-cache-hit | windows-amd-deferred) + `encoder.runtimeError` + `encoder.backPressure`. UI MUST surface selected backend + fallback indicator in the recording status bar at all times.

Mid-session encoder switching is forbidden. On encoder-runtime-error: end the session, mark cached HW path negative, surface error. The user retries; the cached negative routes them straight to libx264 with the fallback indicator. Three clicks, full transparency.

T-006 consumption contract (binding): EncoderBackend exposes `init_segment() -> Bytes` once and a channel of `EncodedFragment { fragment_index, pts_start_90k, pts_end_90k, duration_90k, is_keyframe_first, moof_offset_in_buf, mdat_offset_in_buf, bytes, sample_table: Vec<SampleEntry> }`. T-006 does not parse NAL units; encoder layer is the only thing that touches them. Back-pressure semantics: SegmentSink::push_fragment returns Pending when disk queue full; encoder drops oldest unflushed fragment (replay buffer prioritises recency) and increments back-pressure counter.

Deferred / out of scope: AV1 (any vendor), AMF on Windows, HDR end-to-end tone-mapping policy, user-facing rate-control overrides, audio encode, macOS VideoToolbox, mid-session encoder reconfig beyond IDR forcing, per-source encoder choice in multi-stream.

Validation cases enumerated in N-004 §20 (probe phase, live capture, fragment/segment contract, export/finalisation, fallback transparency) -- feed T-009.

Open implementation items (not blockers): ffmpeg-the-library vs direct vendor bindings, fMP4 muxer choice (movenc default), CUDA context sharing, VAAPI driver deny-list. Pinned at T-005 implementation ticket.
title: Design encoder backend matrix and fallback policy
